extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical philosophy and political theory (readers of Aristotle)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for political science, legislation, and the formation of virtuous character—covering what constitutes the best life, the role of laws/education, and what qualities a legislator or statesman must have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Happiness as Contemplative Speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Happiness then is co-extensive with this Contemplative Speculation; and in proportion as people have the act of Contemplation so far have they also the being happy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that the highest form of human life (happiness) is the life of pure intellect/contemplation, akin to the gods' activity; contemplation is 'in itself precious' and confers supreme blessedness. This view supports privileging theoretical/scientific life over merely moral/political activity when judging the chief good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superiority of life in accordance with Pure Intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: If pure Intellect, as compared with human nature, is divine, so too will the life in accordance with it be divine compared with man’s ordinary life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The life of the pure intellect is 'higher than mere human nature' because it partakes of a divine principle; thus when evaluating lives, prefer those dominated by intellectual activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral (active) life is second-best
rubrics_metrics.description: Second in degree of Happiness will be that Life which is in accordance with the other kind of Excellence... I mean, we do actions of justice, courage, and the other virtues, towards one another...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral virtues (justice, courage, liberality, temperance) constitute a properly human active life that yields happiness, but this life depends more on external goods and social conditions than contemplative life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union of Practical Wisdom and Moral Virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical Wisdom and Excellence of the Moral character are very closely united; since the Principles of Practical Wisdom are in accordance with the Moral Virtues and these are right when they accord with Practical Wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging moral character or actions, assess whether moral virtues are guided by practical wisdom (phronesis); virtue without right practical reasoning is defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: External goods required to a limited extent for Happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: It would seem, moreover, to require supply of external goods to a small degree, or certainly less than the Moral Happiness... neither Self-sufficiency, nor Action, stand in Excess, and it is quite possible to act nobly without being ruler of sea and land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Happiness (especially contemplative) needs some health, nourishment, and minimal external prosperity, but only moderate means are necessary; excess external goods are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific virtues demand specific external conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberal man must have money to do his liberal actions with, and the just man to meet his engagements... the brave man must have power... the man of perfected self-mastery must have opportunity of temptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the practicability/perfection of particular virtues by checking whether the agent has the external resources/opportunities needed to exercise them; absence of these conditions limits full expression of the virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfection of virtuous action requires both choice and action
rubrics_metrics.description: A question is sometimes raised, whether the moral choice or the actions have most to do with Virtue, since it consists in both: it is plain that the perfection of virtuous action requires both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess virtue by both internal deliberation/choice and the actual performance of appropriate actions; ideal moral evaluation considers both aspects together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of virtuous character depends on nature, custom, and teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: The formation of a virtuous character some ascribe to Nature, some to Custom, and some to Teaching... Nature’s part obviously does not rest with us, but belongs to those who in the truest sense are fortunate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing education or reform, consider interplay of innate disposition, social/customary conditioning, and instruction; some elements are beyond deliberate control and must be accommodated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of habituation and early training
rubrics_metrics.description: For he that lives in obedience to passion cannot hear any advice that would dissuade him... there must be, to begin with, a kind of affinity to Virtue in the disposition; which must cleave to what is honourable and loath what is disgraceful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective moral education requires early habituation (soil must be prepared); laws and upbringing should shape likes/dislikes so that virtuous choices are natural rather than merely theoretical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawgivers should regulate food and manner of living
rubrics_metrics.description: The food, and manner of living generally, ought to be the subject of legal regulation, because things when become habitual will not be disagreeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public policy aimed at virtue should include regulation of daily habits (diet, lifestyle) to produce stable virtuous dispositions; examples: Sparta's provisioning and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use compulsion/punishment for the baser sort; honour for the well-trained
rubrics_metrics.description: They should impose chastisement and penalties on those who disobey and are of less promising nature; and the incurable expel entirely: because the good man and he who lives under a sense of honour will be obedient to reason; and the baser sort... will be kept in check, like beasts of burthen by pain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing laws, distinguish audiences: rely on exhortation/honour for the cultured, and on penalties/compulsion for those not responsive to reason; tailor sanctions to be contrary to the pleasures people seek.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law's authority derives from Practical Wisdom and has compelling power
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law has power to compel, since it is a declaration emanating from Practical Wisdom and Intellect. And people feel enmity towards their fellow-men who oppose their impulses, however rightly they may do so: the Law, on the contrary, is not the object of hatred, though enforcing right rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the legitimacy/effectiveness of rules by whether they are grounded in practical wisdom and backed by enforceable institutions rather than mere paternal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private training can better address individual cases than public systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Private training has advantages over Public, as in the case of the healing art:... the individual will be most exactly attended to under Private care, because so each will be more likely to obtain what is expedient for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy or educational design should balance general public systems with individualized (private/familial) attention; recognize tradeoffs between standardization and tailored care.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles are necessary but insufficient for practice
rubrics_metrics.description: General maxims are not only said to be but are the object-matter of sciences: still this is no reason against the possibility of a man’s taking excellent care of some one case, though he possesses no scientific knowledge but from experience is exactly acquainted with what happens in each point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess competence by combination of theoretical principles and practical experience; compendia or compilations of laws alone do not make a competent practitioner or legislator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator/Statesman must combine knowledge and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice, however, seems to contribute no little to its acquisition... those who would acquire a knowledge of Statesmanship must have in addition practice... the Sophists... profess to teach, but not one of them practises it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good legislator or statesman should possess both theoretical understanding of polity and substantial practical experience; teaching or compiling laws without practice is inadequate for producing real statesmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate Polities empirically to determine what preserves or destroys communities
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Polities we have collected, ascertain what kind of things preserve or destroy Communities, and what, particular Constitutions; and the cause why some are well and others ill managed...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method for political science: collect constitutions and practices, compare outcomes, and infer which laws/regulations sustain healthy communities; empirical, comparative inquiry is required to judge constitutions and laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish between those fit for moral exhortation and those needing compulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law, on the contrary, is not the object of hatred... the duty would seem to devolve upon each individual to contribute to the cause of Virtue with his own children and friends...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing civic education, aim to cultivate virtue within families and communities; use persuasion for the well-disposed and coercion for those resistant to reason.
